english.title: Do an act to contravene a closure order
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without reasonable excuse,

(A)_[failed to comply with a closure order made by **(..SPECIFY THE COURT..) Magistrates' Court on **(..SPECIFY THE DATE..) in respect of premises, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PREMISES..), in that **(..SPECIFY THE ACT..)]_
(B)_[did an act , namely **(..SPECIFY THE ACT..), in contravention of a closure order made by **(..SPECIFY THE COURT..) Magistrates' Court on **(..SPECIFY THE DATE..) in respect of premises, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PREMISES..)]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 25(5) of the Criminal Justice and Police Act 2001.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See section 28 for the meaning of "closure order".
(ii) This does not apply to liquor licensed premises.

other.penalty:
Three months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
